title: THE INTERPLAY OF PSYCHOLOGY, PHYSIOLOGY AND ARCHITECTURAL DESIGN: AN OVERVIEW

findings.antecedent: environmental danger
findings.consequent: sympathetic nervous system activation (increased heart rate, blood pressure, opened lung airways, slowed non-essential bodily functions)
findings.mechanism: Release of adrenaline, norepinephrine, and cortisol.
findings.quote: When mammals experience danger, the sympathetic division of the autonomic nervous system jumps into action

findings.antecedent: threat neutralized (fight or flight)
findings.consequent: parasympathetic nervous system activation (body returns to resting state, routine metabolic processes reactivate)
findings.mechanism: Parasympathetic division kicks in to restore homeostasis.
findings.quote: the parasympathetic division of the autonomic nervous system kicks into action working to return the body to its resting state

findings.antecedent: objects and places that increased chances for survival (e.g., food, water, shelter, savanna characteristics)
findings.mechanism: Human brains evolutionarily encoded to associate survival with pleasure.
findings.quote: human brains have been encoded to associate a sense of pleasure with objects and places that increased our chances for survival

findings.antecedent: savanna characteristics (advantageously spaced trees, lush countryside, water, food)
findings.quote: The appeal of the savanna was its advantageously spaced trees, the lush countryside, and the water and food it provided

findings.antecedent: characteristics of the savanna
findings.mechanism: Savanna Hypothesis: characteristics are encoded in our brains.
findings.quote: the Savanna Hypothesis suggests the characteristics of the savanna are encoded in our brains

findings.antecedent: chronic stress
findings.consequent: anxiety, insomnia, depression, weakened immune system, muscle pain, heart disease, high blood pressure
findings.quote: Constant or chronic stress can lead to extremely detrimental, and even permanent, mental and physical health issues.

findings.antecedent: prolonged stress
findings.consequent: shortened telomeres, premature cell death, accelerated aging process
findings.quote: prolonged stress physically shortens the parts of chromosomes known as telomeres

findings.antecedent: seeing beautiful design
findings.consequent: sense of pleasure, release of oxytocin, endorphins, DHEA
findings.mechanism: Physiological response in the brain to beauty.
findings.quote: Seeing something we define as beautiful causes us to feel a sense of pleasure; physiologically this results from the release of oxytocin, endorphins and DHEA in our brain

findings.antecedent: architectural elements with patterns similar to survival-beneficial locations for ancestors
findings.quote: Buildings that provide us with a sense of pleasure are those that incorporate the architectural elements our brain recognizes as having similar characteristics or patterns to locations that helped our ancestors survive.

findings.antecedent: similar advantageous patterns in built environment
findings.mechanism: Subconscious pattern recognition linked to survival.
findings.quote: Seeing similar advantageous patterns in our built environment today evokes a similar physiological reaction.

findings.antecedent: chaos or unpredictability (lack of organized pattern)
findings.quote: chaos or unpredictability, the opposite of organized pattern, can negatively impact us physiologically.

findings.antecedent: too many dissimilar elements / cognitive overload
findings.mechanism: Exceeding cognitive processing limits (human cognitive limit is 7 components).
findings.quote: after that it becomes stressful for our brain to try and remember more.

findings.antecedent: like object grouping (patterns, symmetry)
findings.mechanism: Efficient information processing by grouping similar elements.
findings.quote: Such ‘like object grouping' to avoid cognitive overload... is also applicable to the built environment.

findings.antecedent: environments devoid of information / lack of patterns and symmetries
findings.quote: cognitive boredom can induce the same stress response as perceived danger.

findings.antecedent: buildings incorporating Alexander's 15 fundamental properties (e.g., scaling symmetry, levels of scale, local symmetries)
findings.mechanism: Properties mimic nature and prevent information overload.
findings.quote: Alexander proposed that successful buildings are those perceived by humans to have “life”

findings.antecedent: buildings incorporating symmetries, patterns, fundamental properties
findings.consequent: perceived as beautiful, sense of safety, security, well-being, survival, release of oxytocin, endorphins, DHEA, throttled back sympathetic nervous system, restored body/immune system/telomeres
findings.quote: buildings that incorporate these symmetries, patterns and fundamental properties to be more beautiful because our brains have been physiologically conditioned by evolution to associate those patterns with safety, security, well-being and survival.

findings.antecedent: 3x3 grid pattern, symmetry, scaling hierarchy in architecture
findings.mechanism: Brain's processing of patterns and resemblance to facial structure.
findings.quote: Their universally accepted beauty also shows how psychologically impactful the 3 x 3 grid pattern, symmetry and scaling hierarchy are on the human brain.

findings.antecedent: facial recognition
findings.mechanism: Evolutionary development of brain regions for facial recognition (65% of newborn brain).
findings.quote: Facial recognition is one of the paramount survival adaptations of the human race.

findings.antecedent: inverted face pattern
findings.mechanism: Face recognition cells analyze bilateral symmetry on a vertical axis.
findings.quote: humans are less accurate at recognizing faces when the pattern is inverted as opposed to upright

findings.antecedent: upright T-shape pattern resembling facial structure
findings.quote: It was found that the infants were partial to the shapes when they were right side up and most resembled faces

findings.antecedent: architectural forms and patterns resembling 3x3 grid / human face
findings.consequent: physiological reactions similar to infant face preference (positive)
findings.quote: humans subconsciously see faces in certain architectural forms and patterns, stimulating the same physiological reactions

findings.antecedent: absence of natural geometries and structural balance in built environment
findings.mechanism: Lack of evolutionarily preferred patterns triggers stress.
findings.quote: Our bodies signal the absence of natural geometries and structural balance with anxiety and illness

findings.antecedent: small, unstimulating, monotonously repetitive ‘box' design in houses
findings.quote: small, unstimulating houses (i.e., they lacked characteristics that activate our pleasure response)

findings.antecedent: monochromatic colors, poorly placed windows, absence of architectural detail, repetitive styles (Modernism aesthetic)
findings.consequent: sensory deprivation, lack of intellectual stimulation, cold/unwelcoming environment, lack of well-being
findings.mechanism: Lack of sensory and cognitive engagement.
findings.quote: Monochromatic colors, poorly placed windows, an absence of architectural detail, and repetitive styles produced a unique form of sensory deprivation.

findings.antecedent: battered houses, abandoned/dilapidated buildings
findings.mechanism: Environmental cues of danger/neglect trigger stress response.
findings.quote: battered houses and neighborhoods with abandoned and dilapidated buildings make us feel unsafe and evoke a sense of fear and anxiety

findings.antecedent: built environment with variety of independent shops and unique spaces
findings.quote: humans are generally healthier when their built environment contains a variety of independent shops and unique spaces

findings.antecedent: generic Whole Foods building environment
findings.quote: the former environment resulted in the lowest arousal level of the study

findings.antecedent: unique and lively restaurants with open doors and windows environment
findings.quote: the latter produced a high level of excitement

findings.antecedent: small amounts of boredom / cognitive disengagement
findings.quote: even small amounts of boredom can actually induce stress

findings.antecedent: urban design with novelty or change every few seconds
findings.quote: The holy grail in urban design is to produce some kind of novelty or change every few seconds, otherwise, we become cognitively disengaged

findings.antecedent: well-designed buildings (symmetry, patterns, 3x3 grid, savanna-like security)
findings.consequent: release of neurochemicals (pleasure), positive psychological impact
findings.mechanism: Brain's evolutionary response to preferred patterns.
findings.quote: Well-designed buildings that use successful symmetry and patterns like the 3 x 3 grid pattern... cause the release of neurochemicals that make us feel a sense of pleasure

findings.antecedent: poorly maintained buildings/spaces OR dull repetitive buildings
findings.consequent: nervousness, fear, boredom, physiologic stress response
findings.mechanism: Environmental cues of threat or lack of engagement.
findings.quote: Poorly maintained buildings and spaces make us nervous and fearful, while dull repetitive buildings bore us; both cause a physiologic stress response.

findings.antecedent: contact with nature / restorative environments
findings.quote: Merely being in contact with nature and these environments is enough to set this process in motion.

findings.antecedent: architecture and designs incorporating elements of nature
findings.quote: our preference for architecture and designs that incorporate elements of nature

findings.antecedent: proximity/visual connection with plants/animals/people OR built environments mimicking nature (symmetries/patterns)
findings.quote: proximity and visual connection with plants, animals and people; and b) built environments that successfully mimic that natural environment

findings.antecedent: too much nature (overwhelming)
findings.quote: too much nature can evoke a similar stress-type response

findings.antecedent: arousing but unpleasant environment
findings.consequent: feelings of panic/tenseness, sympathetic nervous system activated
findings.quote: When an environment is arousing but unpleasant, we feel panicked and tense, and our sympathetic nervous system is activated.

findings.antecedent: unpleasant but not arousing environment
findings.quote: when the environment is unpleasant but not arousing, we feel unstimulated and bored; boredom... is also a cause of stress.

findings.antecedent: pleasant and arousing environment
findings.quote: pleasant... arousing (making us feel excited and stimulated, causing chemicals like oxytocin to be released)

findings.antecedent: pleasant and not arousing environment
findings.consequent: feelings of pleasant relaxation/peace, smooth autonomic nervous system function
findings.quote: pleasant... not arousing (making us feel pleasantly relaxed and at peace, helping our autonomic nervous system to run smoothly).

findings.antecedent: environment too extreme on arousal spectrum
findings.consequent: uncomfortable feelings, physiological response (seeking arousal reduction/enhancement)
findings.quote: being too extreme on either side causes us to feel uncomfortable which generates a physiological response

findings.antecedent: built environments perceived as most pleasant and least stressful
findings.mechanism: Innate drive for comfort and well-being.
findings.quote: Humans will for this reason seek out built environments that they find to be most pleasant and least stressful.

findings.antecedent: environments providing ample amounts of information to process
findings.quote: we prefer environments that provide us with ample amounts of information to process

findings.antecedent: too much non-reducible information
findings.quote: too much non-reducible information tends to push the arousing environment away from pleasant and closer to unpleasant

findings.antecedent: environment with high coherence, legibility, complexity, mystery
findings.mechanism: Facilitates information processing and engagement (Kaplan's model).
findings.quote: The categories defined in the model (coherence, legibility, complexity and mystery), are believed by Kaplan to increase an individual's preference for a specific environment.

findings.antecedent: viewing pictures of nature
findings.quote: simply viewing pictures of nature had the ability to lessen the effects of exam induced stress

findings.antecedent: hospital room with window overlooking nature (trees)
findings.quote: shortened post-surgical recovery times for patients in hospital rooms with a window overlooking a small stand of trees

findings.antecedent: viewing 10-minute color video of everyday nature (after stress inducer)
findings.consequent: increased positive feelings, lower blood pressure, lower muscle tension, lower skin conductance levels
findings.quote: The participants exposed to the nature video experienced an increase in positive feelings and were found to have lower blood pressure, muscle tension, and skin conductance levels

findings.antecedent: viewing 10-minute color video of urban areas (after stress inducer)
findings.mechanism: Lack of restorative properties in urban scenes.
findings.quote: the urban scenes failed to produce any of these positive physiologic effects

findings.antecedent: architecture incorporating natural environment
findings.quote: architecture that incorporates the natural environment can facilitate similar restorative effects.

findings.antecedent: personal shelter providing refuge (safe sheltered place) and prospect (unobstructed view of surrounding environment)
findings.consequent: sense of safety, positive psychological impact
findings.mechanism: Evolutionary preference for safe vantage points.
findings.quote: provides us with refuge (a safe sheltered place) and prospect (an unobstructed view of the surrounding environment)

findings.antecedent: windows with view of nature / large windows/glass walls with unobstructed view of nature / indoor plants
findings.quote: houses that have large windows or glass walls permitting an unobstructed view of nature... will be the most beneficial at producing the desired psychological benefits.

findings.antecedent: natural landscapes adapted into built environment
findings.consequent: development of attachment / sense of rootedness to that space
findings.quote: Adaption of such natural landscapes into our built environment is also an essential part of developing an attachment

findings.antecedent: bland and featureless urban architecture
findings.consequent: low level stress, insufficient mental stimulation
findings.quote: Urban architecture is often bland and featureless which we now know creates low level stress and results in insufficient mental stimulation.

findings.antecedent: urban areas devoid of natural environment elements
findings.quote: Urban areas are also frequently devoid of elements of the natural environment which not only creates further stress
